transcript:
Fireflies.ai - Meeting Transcript

Title: Standard Demo v1 - Internal Dry Run #3 (Dedicated + Fallback Routing)
Date: Jun 6, 2025 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 43 min
Recorded by: Fireflies.ai

Attendees:
- Markus Klein (Redwood, Solutions Engineering)
- Soojin Lee (Redwood, Product Marketing)
- Simran Kaur (Redwood, Demo Scenario Architect)
- Colin O'Donnell (Redwood, Demo Integrations)
- Mina Haddad (Redwood, Routing/Fallback)
- Chloe Martin (Redwood, Console Dashboards)
- Sean Gallagher (Redwood, SRE)

Auto-Summary (generated):
- Team rehearsed the Dedicated capacity portion of the standard demo and practiced triggering a controlled fallback from a dedicated pool to the hosted tier.
- Biggest friction was Console navigation: multiple places show “routing” concepts and it was unclear where to click to show the fallback policy quickly.
- Agreed to reduce live clicking by using a direct saved view link and a CLI backup to show route configuration if Console loads slowly.

Topics:
1) Dedicated pool vs hosted tier framing (what we say vs what we show)
2) Route policy + fallback configuration in Console
3) Live failover trigger (simulate capacity constraint)
4) Observability proof (latency, 5xx/429, and failover events)
5) Talk track edits + contingency plan

Action items:
- Soojin: rewrite the narration so the clickpath is one step ("Routes" first) and remove "Rollouts" reference from the Dedicated segment.
- Chloe: create a saved view (or pinned page) for the demo route that surfaces fallback + recent events.
- Colin: add a one-command CLI backup to print route policy + recent routing events for the demo tenant.
- Mina: validate label names and where fallback is configured (policy level vs route level) and send screenshots.
- Sean: confirm demo-tenant alerting won’t page on the intentional failover, and define the acceptable error budget for the demo.

Transcript:

[00:00] Markus Klein: Alright, cool. This is dry run three. The goal is the Dedicated segment plus the fallback routing. We’re gonna do it like we’re on a prospect call, but please interrupt when stuff is confusing.

[00:14] Soojin Lee: And I’ll call out where the deck has screenshots versus where we’re improvising.

[00:18] Simran Kaur: I have the scenario doc open. We’re doing the “dedicated route + fallback to hosted” scenario, right?

[00:24] Markus Klein: Yep. Exactly. Okay, I’m sharing my screen. This is the demo tenant Console.

[00:32] Chloe Martin: Quick reminder, the Console is a little slow this morning. It’s not terrible, but don’t do five clicks if you can do one.

[00:38] Markus Klein: Yeah, heard. Okay, starting like: “Most teams start on a hosted API, but as they scale, they need predictable throughput and isolation.” Then we introduce Dedicated.

[00:52] Soojin Lee: Can you say “reserved capacity” once? Platform folks like that.

[00:55] Markus Klein: Yep. “Reserved capacity, dedicated GPU pool.” Okay. Now I’m going to Routes.

[01:05] Markus Klein: Uh— wait. I’m in… Models. I clicked the left nav wrong.

[01:09] Soojin Lee: This is the thing. In the deck I say “go to Routes” but in Console it’s like, “Traffic” then “Routes”? Or is that in the new nav only?

[01:16] Chloe Martin: In this tenant it’s left nav “Routing” and then “Routes.” But the icon is super similar to “Rollouts,” so people click the wrong one.

[01:23] Markus Klein: Okay, I see “Routing.” Clicking that. Now “Routes.” Great.

[01:30] Markus Klein: So we have a route called “demo-chat-prod” and it’s pinned to… I’m gonna open it.

[01:38] Markus Klein: Here I want to show the policy: prefer dedicated pool, fallback if error or latency…

[01:45] Mina Haddad: Just be careful on the words. It’s not “latency” fallback in this build, it’s “capacity unavailable” and “5xx threshold,” plus manual failover toggle.

[01:54] Markus Klein: Perfect, thank you. So, I’m looking for “Fallback policy.” Where is it.

[02:01] Markus Klein: I see “Routing policy” and “Targets.” There’s “Primary target: dedicated-pool-a” and “Secondary: hosted-tier-usw2.”

[02:10] Colin O'Donnell: That might be enough. Like you can just narrate “primary is dedicated, secondary is hosted.” You don’t need the subpage.

[02:17] Soojin Lee: But the slide says “automated fallback with guardrails.” We should show the guardrails at least once.

[02:22] Markus Klein: Exactly. I want to show it’s not just a list. Okay, there’s a tab “Policies.” Clicking.

[02:30] Markus Klein: (pause) It’s loading.

[02:34] Chloe Martin: This is the load that kills the vibe in a live demo.

[02:37] Markus Klein: Yeah. Okay, “Policies” shows: “Retry,” “Timeout,” “Fallback.” Great. Fallback is collapsed.

[02:45] Markus Klein: Expanding fallback. It says “Trigger: primary unavailable (capacity) OR 5xx rate > 2% for 1 min.” Then “Fail back: auto after 10 min stable.”

[02:58] Mina Haddad: Minor correction: the UI says “server errors” not “five ex ex.” But yeah.

[03:03] Soojin Lee: The phrasing we should use: “If the dedicated pool is constrained or degraded, Redwood keeps your app online by routing to a compatible hosted target.”

[03:12] Markus Klein: Got it. Now I’ll do the show part: send a request and then force a fallback.

[03:18] Simran Kaur: Use the canned prompt so output doesn’t go weird.

[03:22] Markus Klein: Yep. I’m opening the “Requests” panel— where is it. Is it under “Playground”?

[03:29] Colin O'Donnell: For the demo tenant we used the API tab, not Playground, because Playground sometimes caches old settings.

[03:35] Markus Klein: Right. I’ll use the curl script. Okay, terminal.

[03:39] Markus Klein: Running: curl to /v1/chat/completions, model “redwood-llama-… dedicated profile.” Streaming on.

[03:48] Markus Klein: Output is streaming. Good.

[03:51] Soojin Lee: While it streams, narrate what they’re seeing: steady tokens, low latency.

[03:56] Markus Klein: Yep. “Streaming responses, predictable token delivery.” Okay.

[04:03] Markus Klein: Now, to trigger fallback. Mina, remind me, are we doing the manual toggle or the capacity simulation.

[04:09] Mina Haddad: For a dry run do manual toggle. Capacity simulation is flaky. Manual toggle is under the route— but again it’s in a weird place.

[04:17] Markus Klein: That’s… what I’m worried about. Okay, I’m back in the route page. I’m looking for “Failover.”

[04:26] Markus Klein: I don’t see it. I see “Targets,” “Policies,” “Metrics,” “History.”

[04:31] Chloe Martin: It’s in “History” as “Route events” with a button “Initiate failover.” Which is… not intuitive.

[04:38] Soojin Lee: Wait, we’re going to click “History” mid-demo? That sounds risky.

[04:42] Markus Klein: Yeah, also it reads like audit log, not control.

[04:46] Mina Haddad: Totally. That’s the known UX issue. There’s an open thing to move it. For now, you can do it from the “Targets” kebab menu too. Three dots next to the dedicated target.

[04:57] Markus Klein: Okay, three dots. I see “Drain,” “Disable,” “Force fallback.” Okay, “Force fallback.”

[05:05] Markus Klein: Confirm. Done.

[05:09] Markus Klein: Now I run the request again, same curl. And we should see it route to hosted.

[05:16] Colin O'Donnell: Add the header output. The script prints the “x-redwood-route-target” header.

[05:20] Markus Klein: Yep, good call. Running.

[05:25] Markus Klein: It prints: x-redwood-route-target: hosted-tier-usw2. Great.

[05:31] Soojin Lee: That’s good. That’s a clean proof.

[05:34] Markus Klein: Now I want to show observability: “you can see the fallback event and impact.” Chloe, where do I go.

[05:41] Chloe Martin: In Console, if you go to Observability > Routes, there’s a saved view for this route. But again it’s like three levels deep.

[05:49] Markus Klein: This is the part I always lose people. I click Observability… okay.

[05:56] Markus Klein: I’m in “Overview.” I see “Latency,” “Cost per 1k tokens,” “Errors.” How do I filter by route.

[06:04] Chloe Martin: Right side: filter icon. Route = demo-chat-prod. Time range last 15 minutes.

[06:11] Markus Klein: Found it. Okay, now I see a spike in “fallback events” panel. Nice.

[06:18] Sean Gallagher: Careful: on the live tenant, that panel sometimes lags by like a minute. If you wait for it, you’ll dead-air.

[06:25] Markus Klein: Good point. So I should narrate like “we also have dashboards; we’ll send you screenshots.” But we want to show it live at least once.

[06:33] Soojin Lee: Or show the “Route events” table instead of the chart? Tables load faster.

[06:38] Chloe Martin: The events table is under the route “History” page, which we just said is confusing.

[06:44] Markus Klein: Yeah. This is the trade.

[06:47] Mina Haddad: I’d do: show the header proving it routed to hosted. That’s the “hard proof.” Then optionally go to dashboard if it’s fast.

[06:55] Simran Kaur: And if asked, you can say “we alert on this and can auto-failback.”

[07:00] Markus Klein: Okay, continuing talk track: “This is how we keep your app online, without you writing custom retry logic.”

[07:07] Soojin Lee: Add: “And you can pin versions so demos and prod don’t change on you.”

[07:12] Markus Klein: Yep. Now let me do the Dedicated story: “Dedicated gives isolation and predictable throughput.” I should show the dedicated pool page.

[07:21] Markus Klein: Where is that? Is it under “Capacity”?

[07:24] Chloe Martin: Left nav “Deployments” then “Dedicated.” It used to be “Capacity.”

[07:30] Markus Klein: That’s… okay. See, even internally we don’t know.

[07:35] Soojin Lee: In the deck we have a screenshot and we say “Dedicated Pools.” We should align the name.

[07:40] Mina Haddad: It is “Dedicated Deployments” in the UI right now.

[07:44] Markus Klein: Okay, clicking Deployments > Dedicated.

[07:50] Markus Klein: I see “dedicated-pool-a” with GPUs, utilization, queue depth. Great. That’s the proof of reserved capacity.

[07:58] Sean Gallagher: Don’t linger on utilization. If it’s at 2% you’ll get a question like “why am I paying for idle.”

[08:04] Markus Klein: Good call. I’ll just show it exists and has isolation.

[08:09] Colin O'Donnell: Also the queue depth is the best proof point: it shows you can absorb bursts.

[08:13] Markus Klein: Great.

[08:16] Markus Klein: Okay, I’m going to recap segment like: “Start hosted, graduate to dedicated, add fallback. Same API.”

[08:24] Soojin Lee: Can you do the “choose your adventure” line? Like “If you need VPC, we go Private.”

[08:29] Markus Klein: Yes. “And if you need VPC isolation or on-prem, we deploy the same control plane privately.”

[08:36] Simran Kaur: One more: For platform engineers, they’ll ask “how do I control when it fails over.” You showed that. But they’ll also ask “can I block fallback to avoid compliance issues.”

[08:46] Mina Haddad: Yes, you can set secondary targets only within allowed regions/tiers. But don’t overpromise cross-region if the demo tenant only has US.

[08:55] Markus Klein: Great. So I’ll say: “fallback targets are policy-controlled; you can restrict by region and deployment mode.”

[09:03] Soojin Lee: Phrase it as “policy guardrails.”

[09:06] Markus Klein: Okay.

[09:08] Markus Klein: Let’s do a quick Q&A simulation. Soojin, ask me the annoying question.

[09:13] Soojin Lee: Sure. “How do I know you won’t silently route my traffic somewhere I didn’t approve?”

[09:19] Markus Klein: Answer: “You set the allowed targets. And we log routing decisions. You can see events and audit logs.”

[09:27] Sean Gallagher: Careful: audit logs is a loaded word. For demo tenant we have route events and console history. Audit logs are in enterprise package.

[09:34] Markus Klein: Good catch. So say “event history” and “exportable logs.”

[09:38] Soojin Lee: Right, and then “for formal audit logging, we integrate with SIEM in enterprise.”

[09:44] Markus Klein: Great.

[09:46] Colin O'Donnell: Another common one: “Is fallback instant or do we get 500s first?”

[09:51] Markus Klein: We should be honest: “There can be a brief blip depending on trigger, but the point is graceful degradation.”

[09:58] Mina Haddad: Exactly. Don’t say zero errors. Say “bounded impact.” And show the policy triggers.

[10:04] Markus Klein: Great.

[10:06] Chloe Martin: Can we talk about the clickpath confusion explicitly? Because that’s what broke in dry run #2.

[10:12] Markus Klein: Yep. The confusion for me: (1) where to find fallback policy quickly, (2) where the “force fallback” control is, and (3) where to find the event proof.

[10:23] Soojin Lee: And the deck currently says: “Console > Rollouts > Routing policy.” Which is wrong.

[10:30] Chloe Martin: Yeah, Rollouts is separate. If you go there you’ll never find fallback.

[10:34] Markus Klein: So action: update talk track to say “Routing > Routes > demo-chat-prod > Policies.” That’s the one sentence.

[10:42] Soojin Lee: Agree. And I’ll add a speaker note: “If Console is slow, prove fallback via response header.”

[10:49] Colin O'Donnell: I’ll add a script that prints: route target header + request id, so you can cross-reference later.

[10:55] Sean Gallagher: And as SRE note: if you’re going to force fallback in the tenant, make sure you restore it. Otherwise the next AE demo is going to be on hosted and they’ll think dedicated is broken.

[11:06] Simran Kaur: That’s why the reset checklist exists, but nobody runs it.

[11:11] Markus Klein: Okay, we’ll bake it into the pre-demo ritual.

[11:14] Markus Klein: Let’s continue with the rest of the dry run like we’re finishing the call. “We saw dedicated plus fallback. Next we can run a benchmark.”

[11:23] Soojin Lee: And “what success looks like” plus next steps.

[11:26] Markus Klein: Exactly.

[11:28] Markus Klein: “Next step: we’ll set you up with an eval tenant or a short POC. We’ll run your prompt set and compare latency/cost.”

[11:38] Colin O'Donnell: Also mention: “we can pin model versions for the POC so results don’t drift.”

[11:43] Markus Klein: Yep.

[11:45] (Cross-talk)

[11:46] Chloe Martin: Wait— can we actually flip it back now to dedicated primary? I don’t want this stuck.

[11:51] Markus Klein: Good call. Going back to route. Targets. Three dots. “Stop fallback” / “Re-enable primary.” Clicking.

[12:00] Markus Klein: Confirmed. It says “Primary active.” Great.

[12:05] Sean Gallagher: Thank you.

[12:07] Markus Klein: Alright. Anything else we need to capture.

[12:11] Mina Haddad: One more thing: don’t say “automatic region failover” in this segment. We are doing target failover within a route. Region is separate policy.

[12:19] Soojin Lee: Good catch. I’ll remove “region” wording from that slide note.

[12:23] Markus Klein: And competitor mention: if asked “How is this different from Bedrock?” we say: “more control on routing and observability across hosted/dedicated/private.”

[12:33] Soojin Lee: And “economics: batching/caching, token-level cost.”

[12:36] Markus Klein: Yep.

[12:38] Markus Klein: Okay I think we got what we needed. We’ll send around action items.

[12:44] Soojin Lee: Please send me the exact clickpath line. I’ll update the master script today.

[12:48] Colin O'Donnell: And I’ll PR the CLI backup snippet.

[12:51] Chloe Martin: I’ll generate a saved view link and drop it in the runbook.

[12:55] Sean Gallagher: I’ll check alerts and make sure forced fallback doesn’t page the demo channel.

[13:00] Markus Klein: Great, thanks all.

(Transcript ends early; remainder of meeting contained off-record screen sharing and navigation testing.)
